cards.when: a panel (i,t); estimating one equation with a test for unit/time effects (within/random/pooling/between/fd)
cards.when_not: a lagged dependent variable on the RHS (Nickell bias -> #47 GMM); small-N/large-T; panel unit-root/cointegration (01/other categories)

alternatives.criterion: a dynamic panel / endogenous regressors
hierarchical shrinkage / non-gaussian / a full posterior
the cross-sectional long-run relation only

output_key_fields: coefficients: named vector of regressor effects (within = within-unit)
coef_table: Estimate/SE/t/p — the SE correspond to the vcov that was supplied
vcov: ALWAYS non-robust; rvcov: the robust one (absent when it was not requested)
ercomp: the random-effects variance components + theta (theta->0 ~ pooling, ->1 ~ fixed effects); absent for the other models
hausman_test/lm_test/f_test: flat records {statistic, p_value, parameter, method}
interpretation_traps: robust inference: read the SE from rvcov/coef_table, NOT from vcov (always non-robust)
FE vs RE is a Hausman test, not an assumption; reject -> FE
the within R² is measured in the transformed space — not comparable with the pooling R²
pd_fixed_effects only for within, pd_random_effects only for random (explicit gates)
panelmodel-interface tests: a pgmm object is deliberately blocked (otherwise LAPACK singular)
sources: Baltagi 2013 Econometric Analysis of Panel Data 5th ed. §4.3
precondition_tools: pd_hausman_test (FE vs RE: reject H0 -> FE)

cards.method: Dynamic panel GMM (Arellano-Bond difference / Blundell-Bond system)
cards.when: a dynamic panel (lagged dependent / endogenous regressors), large-N small-T; diff-GMM (transformation=d) or system-GMM (ld)
cards.when_not: static, without a lagged dependent variable -> #46; small-N/large-T; instrument proliferation (Sargan p~1)

alternatives.criterion: T is large (Nickell bias negligible) or there is no lagged dependent variable
a persistent/near-unit-root dependent variable (weak instruments in the differences)
joint dynamics of many equations

output_key_fields: coefficients: named; the lag(y) coefficient = persistence (must be <1)
coef_table: Estimate/SE/z/p — with robust=True and two-step estimation the SE are Windmeijer-corrected
sargan_test: the overidentification record, H0 = the instruments are valid (you want a large p)
autocorr_test1/autocorr_test2: the Arellano-Bond m1/m2 serial-correlation records
residuals: a list per individual (not a flat vector); fitted: numeric
interpretation_traps: Sargan: a large p is good (valid); p~1.00 signals instrument proliferation (use collapse=True)
m1/AR(1) is expected to be significant (normal, due to differencing) — NOT a problem
m2/AR(2) must NOT be rejected; rejection -> the moment conditions are invalid
two-step standard errors without the Windmeijer correction (robust=False) are severely downward-biased
the documented df_residual is not present on the fitted object — it is not exposed
precondition_tools: pd_gmm_autocorr_test (post: AR(2)/m2 MUST NOT be rejected)

cards.method: Fixed-Effects Individual-Slopes (FEIS) + a slope-heterogeneity Hausman test (artificial & bootstrapped)
cards.when: a panel (i,t) where the effect of a trend/slope variable (e.g. time/experience) differs by unit; you want consistency even when the unit-specific slope is correlated with the regressors (detrending instead of demeaning)
cards.when_not: no theoretical slope heterogeneity (conventional FE #46 suffices); fewer than q+1 observations per unit (q=the number of slope parameters); a dynamic panel / lagged dependent variable (Nickell -> #47 GMM); time-invariant regressors of interest (detrending removes them)

alternatives.criterion: no slope heterogeneity; feis_test art1 does not reject
a dynamic panel / endogenous regressors
hierarchical shrinkage of the slopes / a full posterior / non-gaussian

output_key_fields: coefficients: a named vector of regressor effects in the detrended space
coef_table: Estimate/Std. Error/t-value/Pr(>|t|); the standard errors are robust when robust=True (vcov_arg records it)
slopevars: the slope variables (the right-hand side of '|'); r2 and adj_r2 in the detrended space; n_groups after dropping units with fewer than q+1 observations
feis_test/feis_bootstrap_test: art_feis_vs_fe / art_fe_vs_re / art_feis_vs_re = {chi2, df, p_value}; the ones not requested are absent
slopes (feis_slopes): an N x J matrix of alpha_i indexed by unit id; it includes the intercept
interpretation_traps: the coefficients/r2 are in the DETRENDED space — not directly comparable with within/pooling FE
art1 (FEIS vs FE) rejection -> the slope heterogeneity matters; do NOT fall back to conventional FE
feis silently drops units with <q+1 observations (a warning); check n_groups against the original N
time-invariant regressors vanish under the detrending — they are not estimated here
feis_bootstrap_test is STOCHASTIC (a pairs-cluster bootstrap); the same seed -> the same p (seed=2025 by default); a low number of reps gives a noisy p
feis_test and feis_bootstrap_test return nothing for the components outside the selected type (art1/bs1 give only art_feis_vs_fe)
sources: Ruettenauer & Ludwig 2020, Sociological Methods & Research (FEIS), doi:10.1177/0049124120926211
Bruederl & Ludwig 2015, Sage Handbook of Regression Analysis §Fixed-Effects Panel Regression
Wooldridge 2010 Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data 2nd ed. §10.7 (regression-based Hausman), §11 (heterogeneous slopes)
Mundlak 1978 (Econometrica 46:69) — the CRE specification behind feistest
precondition_tools: feis_test (a regression-based Hausman test: rejecting art1 -> FEIS over FE)
feis_bootstrap_test (the bootstrapped Hausman test; more reliable at small N)
c08_panel_data/static_panel_estimators.pd_hausman_test (the classic FE vs RE test before considering slope heterogeneity)

cards.method: Beck-Katz Panel-Corrected Standard Errors (PCSE) for pooled TSCS/OLS
cards.when: pooled OLS on time-series cross-section data (N units × T periods, with T not << N); you want SE robust to panel heteroskedasticity + contemporaneous (cross-unit) correlation, keeping the OLS coefficients
cards.when_not: a lagged dependent variable / endogeneity (Nickell bias -> #47 GMM); within/random effects (#46); an N >> T micro panel (prefer clustered/Driscoll-Kraay); serial correlation as the main problem (Prais-Winsten/Newey-West)

alternatives.criterion: unit-specific effects correlated/uncorrelated with the regressors — FE/RE instead of pooling
N >> T or strong cross-sectional dependence with a large N
Beck-Katz PCSE inside a panel model rather than on a pooled least-squares fit

output_key_fields: coefficients: a named vector of OLS coefficients (they do NOT change under the PCSE correction)
coef_table: Estimate/PCSE/t value/Pr(>|t|) — the SE are panel-corrected
pcse: a named vector of the panel-corrected SE; vcov: the full PCSE covariance matrix
df/nobs/nmiss: degrees of freedom, valid observations, missing panel cells
pairwise: True = pairwise, False = casewise; balanced: no missing cells
interpretation_traps: PCSE corrects ONLY the SE — the coefficients remain pooled OLS (non-robust point estimates)
casewise (pairwise=False) uses only the balanced rectangle; on a heavily unbalanced panel set pairwise=True
an unset pairwise flag runs silently wrong — the wrapper blocks it explicitly
Beck-Katz assumes T is not << N; with N >> T the PCSE are unreliable -> Driscoll-Kraay/clustered
vcov = the PCSE covariance (NOT the classical OLS vcov); read the inference from coef_table/pcse
gaps in the model or index columns drop rows inside the fit -> a length mismatch; the wrapper requires complete cases
sources: Beck & Katz 1995, 'What to Do (and Not to Do) with Time-Series Cross-Section Data', APSR 89(3):634-647
Beck 2001, Annual Review of Political Science 4:271-293 (TSCS practice)
precondition_tools: pcse_fit (it produces the pcse object; all it needs is formula+data+index)
c01_preparation_prechecks/panel_unit_root.run_panel_unit_root (a panel unit-root test for a large-T macro panel before pooled OLS)

cards.method: Hierarchical / multilevel (mixed) models — linear & generalized (partial pooling)
cards.when: hierarchical/nested data (e.g. regions within countries, years within units); you want partial pooling — random intercepts/slopes per group with shrinkage — instead of full pooling or entirely separate models per group
cards.when_not: the group effects are correlated with the regressors (endogeneity -> the within estimator, #46); a lagged dependent variable on the right-hand side (Nickell bias -> #47); a single hierarchical level with no repeated sampling; you want a full Bayesian posterior with priors (-> #69, category 14)

alternatives.criterion: the individual effects are correlated with the regressors -> partial pooling causes bias, use FE
one level, linear, a panel (i,t); GLS variance components suffice without the full mixed-model machinery
you want priors / a full posterior / a more complex likelihood, or hierarchical shrinkage with uncertainty quantification

output_key_fields: fixef: a named vector of population-level (fixed) coefficients
coef_table: Estimate/Std.Error/t (lmer) or +z/Pr(>|z|) (glmer) — NOTE: lmer gives NO p-value by design
varcorr: long-format records {grp,var1,var2,vcov,sdcor} — the variance/covariance/correlation of the random effects
sigma: the residual scale (== the residual scale of the variance components); ngrps: the number of groups per grouping factor; nobs
ranef: records {grpvar,term,grp,condval,condsd} — the BLUPs (shrunk group deviations) + the conditional SD
log_lik/AIC/BIC: model fit (AIC/BIC are comparable only ML-vs-ML; REML likelihoods are NOT comparable across different fixed effects)

singular (the logical isSingular)/converged (logical)/conv_messages (char): they record degeneracy & convergence IN THE SAME output — under a stateless node contract stderr is lost, so check these instead of relying on warnings
interpretation_traps: REML=True likelihoods are NOT comparable across models with different fixed effects — for a likelihood-ratio test or AIC on the fixed effects set REML=False (plain ML)

the linear mixed fit returns NO p-values (there is no default degrees-of-freedom convention) — coef_table carries only the t value; judge significance with an interval or a likelihood-ratio test, never from a p that does not exist
ranef are conditional modes (BLUPs), NOT parameters — they are shrunk towards 0; do NOT read them as separate fixed effects per group

a 'boundary (singular) fit' (the group standard deviation goes to 0) means the random effect is not supported by the data — too few groups, or zero between-group variance; the wrapper records it explicitly as singular=True, and it must not be ignored: the variance components are degenerate
partial pooling presupposes random effects UNCORRELATED with the regressors (as in RE/Hausman) — otherwise prefer within/FE (#46)
the family of lme_fit_glm is a closed enum; gaussian is NOT allowed there (use lme_fit)
sources: Bates, Mächler, Bolker & Walker 2015 JSS 67(1) (fitting linear mixed-effects models)
Gelman & Hill 2007, Data Analysis Using Regression and Multilevel/Hierarchical Models
Pinheiro & Bates 2000, Mixed-Effects Models in S and S-PLUS (BLUP/partial pooling)
precondition_tools: lme_fit (a linear response; register the model handle for ranef/varcorr)
lme_fit_glm (a non-gaussian response: binomial, poisson, Gamma or inverse-gaussian)
c08_panel_data/static_panel_estimators.pd_fit (comparison: FE/within when the effects are endogenous)

cards.method: Correlated random effects: Mundlak and Hausman-Taylor
cards.when: you want the efficiency of random effects and the consistency of fixed effects, or you need coefficients on time-invariant regressors that fixed effects wipes out
cards.when_not: there are no time-invariant regressors of interest and fixed effects is adequate; no valid instruments exist for Hausman-Taylor

alternatives.criterion: consistency and no time-invariant coefficients needed
a transparent way to allow correlated effects
time-invariant coefficients wanted and some regressors are exogenous

output_key_fields: params: including coefficients on time-invariant regressors
mundlak_test: joint test of the group means, which is the Hausman test in another form
instrument_validity: over-identification test for Hausman-Taylor
efficiency_gain: against the fixed-effects estimator
interpretation_traps: THE MUNDLAK TEST OF THE GROUP MEANS IS EQUIVALENT TO THE HAUSMAN TEST but is robust and never produces a negative statistic, which the classical Hausman form frequently does
Hausman-Taylor requires you to classify regressors as exogenous or endogenous, and that classification is an assumption the data cannot check
time-invariant coefficients are identified only through that classification, so they are the most fragile numbers in the output

cards.method: Mean group, pooled mean group and common correlated effects
cards.when: the panel has a long time dimension and slopes that plausibly differ across units, where pooling imposes a homogeneity that biases everything
cards.when_not: the time dimension is short, where per-unit estimates are hopeless; homogeneity is credible

alternatives.criterion: fully heterogeneous slopes, averaged
common long run, heterogeneous short run
cross-sectional dependence from unobserved common factors

output_key_fields: params: the averaged or pooled coefficients
unit_coefficients: the per-unit estimates the average rests on
homogeneity_test: test of slope equality across units
cd_test: cross-sectional dependence in the residuals
interpretation_traps: POOLING HETEROGENEOUS SLOPES BIASES THE ESTIMATE, and in dynamic panels it biases the persistence parameter upward severely
the mean group estimator is sensitive to outlying units; a single badly estimated unit can dominate the average
common correlated effects handles factor dependence by augmenting with cross-sectional averages, and needs enough units for those averages to be informative

cards.when: estimating a cross-sectional relationship period by period and averaging, which handles cross-sectional correlation without modelling it
cards.when_not: the cross-section is small, where per-period estimates are noise; the dependence is in the time dimension rather than the cross-section

alternatives.criterion: you want one regression
cross-sectional correlation, many periods
the unobserved heterogeneity is at unit level

output_key_fields: params: the time-series average of the cross-sectional estimates
period_estimates: the per-period coefficients
se: Fama-MacBeth standard errors from their time-series variation
newey_west: autocorrelation-corrected variant
interpretation_traps: FAMA-MACBETH STANDARD ERRORS DO NOT CORRECT FOR TIME-SERIES AUTOCORRELATION of the coefficient estimates; a Newey-West adjustment is needed when the estimates persist
the method handles cross-sectional correlation but assumes the per-period estimates are independent over time, which is often false
with a short time dimension the average rests on few draws and the standard error is unreliable

cards.method: Seemingly unrelated regressions and three-stage least squares
cards.when: several equations share correlated errors, and estimating them jointly is more efficient than one at a time
cards.when_not: the equations have identical regressors, where joint estimation gives exactly the equation-by-equation result

alternatives.criterion: regressors are identical across equations
correlated errors and different regressors
correlated errors and endogenous regressors

output_key_fields: params: coefficients across all equations
residual_correlation: the cross-equation correlation driving the efficiency gain
breusch_pagan: test that the errors are uncorrelated across equations
efficiency_gain: against equation-by-equation estimation
interpretation_traps: IF EVERY EQUATION HAS THE SAME REGRESSORS, SUR IS EXACTLY OLS equation by equation -- there is no gain, and a reported gain means the specification differs from what you think
the efficiency gain comes entirely from the cross-equation error correlation; test it before claiming the gain
a misspecification in one equation contaminates every other equation's estimates under joint estimation

cards.method: Panel quantile regression: Canay and Machado-Santos Silva
cards.when: the covariate effect differs across the conditional distribution and the panel has unobserved heterogeneity that ordinary quantile regression cannot remove
cards.when_not: there is no panel structure; the effect is plainly homogeneous across quantiles

alternatives.criterion: no unit heterogeneity
heterogeneity enters as a location shift
heterogeneity affects both location and scale

output_key_fields: params: coefficients per quantile
quantiles: the levels estimated
crossing: whether fitted quantile curves cross
se: bootstrap standard errors, which are the usual choice here
interpretation_traps: THE FIXED EFFECT CANNOT SIMPLY BE DIFFERENCED OUT of a quantile regression -- the quantile of a difference is not the difference of quantiles, which is why these specialised estimators exist
Canay's two-step assumes the unit effect is a pure location shift, which rules out heterogeneity in dispersion
with a short time dimension the estimated unit effects are noisy and that noise contaminates the second step

cards.method: Panel instrumental variables with high-dimensional fixed effects
cards.when: an endogenous regressor in a panel with several high-dimensional fixed effects to absorb at the same time
cards.when_not: there is no endogeneity; the fixed effects are low dimensional and dummies suffice

alternatives.alt: panel IV with one fixed effect
alternatives.criterion: one dimension only
several dimensions
the panel is dynamic and lags are the instruments

output_key_fields: params: second-stage coefficients
first_stage: relevance diagnostics after absorption
absorbed: the fixed effects removed
cluster: the clustering applied
interpretation_traps: ABSORBING FIXED EFFECTS REMOVES VARIATION FROM THE INSTRUMENT TOO; an instrument strong in levels can be weak after absorption, so the first stage must be recomputed after, not before
the effective first-stage F must account for the absorbed dimensions in its degrees of freedom
clustering at a level finer than the absorbed dimension understates the standard errors
sources: Correia 2017, Linear models with high-dimensional fixed effects (unpublished manuscript)
Wooldridge 2010, Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data, 2nd ed., ch.11

cards.method: Driscoll-Kraay, two-way and multiway clustered standard errors
cards.when: choosing the covariance estimator that matches the dependence the panel actually has, which is where most panel inference goes wrong
cards.when_not: the errors are demonstrably independent; the panel is too small in the relevant dimension for the estimator's asymptotics

alternatives.criterion: dependence within one dimension
dependence within units and within periods
cross-sectional dependence with a long time dimension

output_key_fields: vcov: the covariance matrix
se: standard errors under each requested estimator, side by side
n_clusters: the cluster counts, which determine reliability
comparison: how much the choice moves the standard errors
interpretation_traps: CLUSTERING AT TOO FINE A LEVEL UNDERSTATES STANDARD ERRORS, and the difference between unit-clustered and two-way clustered errors is frequently a factor of two
two-way clustering can produce a non-positive-definite covariance matrix in small samples; the eigenvalue correction changes the answer
Driscoll-Kraay needs a long time dimension and is badly undersized when it is short
sources: Driscoll & Kraay 1998 (Review of Economics and Statistics 80:549-560)
Cameron, Gelbach & Miller 2011 (Journal of Business and Economic Statistics 29:238)

cards.method: Poisson and negative-binomial panel models with high-dimensional fixed effects
cards.when: the outcome is a count or a non-negative quantity with many zeros, in a panel with high-dimensional fixed effects
cards.when_not: the outcome is continuous and unbounded; the fixed effects are low dimensional

alternatives.criterion: non-negative outcome, zeros present, robust to distribution
overdispersion must be modelled explicitly
wrong here whenever zeros are present

output_key_fields: params: coefficients, interpretable as semi-elasticities
dispersion: the overdispersion parameter where estimated
absorbed: the fixed effects removed
separation: observations dropped by perfect separation
interpretation_traps: LOG-LINEARISING A MODEL WITH ZEROS IS NOT A WORKAROUND -- it drops the zeros and biases the estimates; Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood exists precisely for this
Poisson PML is consistent under correct conditional-mean specification even when the outcome is not Poisson, which is why it is the default for trade and count data
perfect separation silently drops observations and fixed-effect groups, changing the estimation sample without warning
sources: Silva & Tenreyro 2006 (Review of Economics and Statistics 88:641-658)

cards.method: Between and within variance decomposition and poolability tests
cards.when: understanding where the variation in a panel actually lies, which determines what any estimator can identify
cards.when_not: the panel has one period or one unit, where the decomposition is degenerate

alternatives.criterion: you want to see where variation lives
you want a formal test of slope homogeneity
the question is fixed against random effects

output_key_fields: between_variance, within_variance: the decomposition per variable
rho: share of variance that is between units
poolability_test: test of common slopes across units
identification_warning: variables with almost no within variation
interpretation_traps: A REGRESSOR WITH ALMOST NO WITHIN VARIATION IS BARELY IDENTIFIED under fixed effects; the coefficient will be huge, imprecise, and meaningless
a high between-share means fixed effects discards most of the information, which is a cost, not automatically the right trade
the poolability test has power against many alternatives and identifies none of them
sources: Baltagi 2021, Econometric Analysis of Panel Data, 6th ed., ch.2-4

cards.method: Attrition tests and inverse probability weighting for unbalanced panels
cards.when: units leave the panel non-randomly, so the balanced subsample is not representative and the unbalanced one is not either
cards.when_not: attrition is negligible; the attrition mechanism depends on unobservables, where weighting cannot help

alternatives.criterion: a formal test that attrition is ignorable
reweight the retained units
attrition depends on unobservables

output_key_fields: attrition_test: test that leavers differ systematically
attrition_probability: the fitted retention model
weights: inverse probability weights for the retained sample
attrition_rate: retention by wave
interpretation_traps: ATTRITION WEIGHTS ONLY FIX SELECTION ON OBSERVABLES; if leaving depends on the unobserved outcome, no weighting scheme repairs it
the balanced subsample is a selected sample, and analysing it 'for consistency' is the most common way attrition bias enters silently
weights estimated from a poorly fitting retention model add variance without removing bias
sources: Becketti, Gould, Lillard & Welch 1988 (Journal of Labor Economics 6:472-492)

cards.method: Two-way fixed effects for matched employer-employee data (AKM)
cards.when: separating worker and firm contributions to pay using mobility between employers -- the standard decomposition in matched administrative data
cards.when_not: there is no mobility between units, where the two effects are not separately identified at all

alternatives.criterion: the standard decomposition
limited mobility bias is material
you are willing to assume effects are uncorrelated

output_key_fields: worker_effects, firm_effects: the estimated effects
variance_decomposition: shares attributable to workers, firms and sorting
connected_set: the largest connected component, the only place effects are identified
limited_mobility_bias: the correction applied
interpretation_traps: LIMITED MOBILITY BIAS is severe: with few movers per firm, the estimated worker-firm covariance is biased downward substantially, which understates sorting
effects are identified only within the CONNECTED SET; units outside it are dropped and the sample changes silently
the decomposition attributes covariance to sorting, and that term is the one most contaminated by estimation error
